title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I received thy kind letter from the Yearly Meeting, which was truly acceptable. & embrace this opportunity in a few words to inform that we are middling well in health, & have been for the most part since we come into this country. Expect about the 1st of the 4th month to move to a place I have lately purchased near 4 miles from Jonas’, & have great cause to acknowledge in humble gratitude & kindness of Providence many ways towards us.

The parting with our Friends in Moorestown (therein particular) I have very often to remember. How I observed in some others what I felt myself, my heart was full, my tongue faltered. It was for some time ere I could utter that very familiar term, farwell. The best of friends must part, Feeling has no fellow. Time hastens on, yet a little while & we shall be as though we had not been, Go to the Land of Darkness & seeing these things are so what manner of persons ought we to be, in all Godliness &. My wishes & desires therefore are, that we may all steadily labor to attain to those happy shores where no troubles annoy.

Since we have been in this country, I have often thought that we have come to the right place & feel well satisfied. Although, we may expect to encounter many difficulties; the country being much unimproved & our society here in a very similar state. I have sometimes thought our society here might be compared to David’s army, which consisted of such who had been in trouble & in debt &. But his men, I apprehend, were under much better discipline than we are.

The plantation we are about to remove to is pretty well improved for this country. A tolerable log house & kitchen, out-houses, barn & stables & several tenements, all of log. A young apple orchard of excellent fruit (they say) & a variety of other fruits & plenty of sugar trees. About 10 acres of very good meadow cleared; the owner allows that he had 400 bushels of wheat last harvest, & a prospect of much more the ensuing season.

I have hopes that with the Blessings of Providence when settled to enjoy a state of contentment, with which if we may be favored or helped to, add Godliness. That will be great gain, for we brought nothing &.

closer.salute: My wife johns in a salutation of kind love to thee & thine, with wishes for your health & welfare every way
